correctness.rationale: Every weak component contains one directed cycle. Summing indicator covariances over the labeled directed cycles and conditioning on their forced outgoing images gives the exact formula. Degree-class probability generating functions use binomial marginals, without assuming independence among the vertices’ degrees. A Gaussian upper bound for cyclic-length weights supplies the Riemann-sum normalization; the postquadratic binomial remainder sums to a compact-uniform term of order inverse square-root sample size. Cauchy coefficient extraction yields the signed Poisson second-difference profile for each fixed degree. Exhaustive enumeration of 873611 labeled maps at sizes two through seven establishes 33 exact-rational comparisons and twelve conservation checks; tests corroborate rather than replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Compared the exact entire covariance generating polynomial and all fixed in-degree limits, rather than the marginal component law or in-degree marginal. Hansen–Jaworski 2006/2008 gives the distribution of components conditional on cyclic vertices and an exchangeable-in-degree framework, not the displayed mixed covariance profile. The 2014 structural-transition paper treats constrained mapping ensembles, not covariance with random in-degree class counts in the unconditioned uniform law. Generic generating-function approaches could imply the formula indirectly; the broad Flajolet–Odlyzko chapter was not fully accessible, so historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: The Flajolet–Odlyzko 1990 broad mapping-statistics chapter could not be fully read; generating-function methods there may implicitly produce equivalent mixed moments.
Some older component-degree joint moment sources or unindexed tables may have implicit coverage.
This same-source and publication comparison does not establish absolute historical priority or independence.

value.rationale: An immediate in-degree histogram is the canonical local profile of a random functional graph, whereas component count records the global cyclic decomposition. Marginals do not determine their covariances. The entire limiting signed Poisson second-difference profile has a natural interpretation constrained by the two deterministic degree conservation identities, with surprising positive correlations at exactly one and two incoming edges and negative correlations in all other fixed degree classes. This is a motivated complete degree-class classification, not a singled-out arbitrary parameter; older cyclic-core negative-zero-degree results are not presented as a separate contribution.
